jobs.title: Living room v3.1.0: re-check every trigger, dead sensor counts as clear and pushes, lux 250/175
jobs.notes: Commits eea93fa and 22ce707. Codex: 2x P1 fixed. HA drops numeric_state for: timers on restart/reload, so start and reload now act on the current lux at once. That means start and reload can turn lights on in an occupied dark room; the 5-min tick still never turns them on. P2 kept: (a) if both sensors are missing, the lights go off at the first trigger rather than after the timeout, but the deploy entity check prevents this; (b) a sensor flipping between unavailable and unknown can push more than once an hour; (c) mode: restart can cancel a push. Decided by orchestrator: no raw lux state trigger, because the tick plus numeric_state triggers cover it and a raw trigger would run about every 44 s. Full suite 1036 passed, plus the 2 old precool failures. Dry run against live states passed. Merge and deploy wait for Martin's OK.

jobs.title: Living room v3.2.0: night window ignores FP300, dim then off
jobs.notes: Commits cf5024c and 266d7fd. Codex: P1 fixed. An FP300 change inside the window reset empty_age, so the tick could re-brighten a dimmed empty room. In the window the FP300's age is now at least the window age. P1 declined: Codex wanted lights to come on at 06:00 when the FP300 still reads on. By design they do not, because that is most likely the dog; a new detection turns them on. This is documented and tested. Decided by orchestrator: inside the window the timeout is always late_night_timeout. An FP300 that is on at the window start counts as clear from the start. The dim is 30 % of the profile target brightness, at least 1 %, with the ceiling scaled. Two template wake triggers fire at window start + L and + L+1 minutes, plus an FP2 timer at L+1. The first Codex run hit the 10-min timeout and was rerun. Full suite 1073 passed, plus the 2 old precool failures. Dry run against live states passed.
jobs.deploy: 2026-11-27 ~08:08 CET: v3.2.0 blueprint and instance deployed. Automation on, live config equals the repo, and the reload trace shows no errors. The dim and wake triggers are not yet seen live; check tonight's 01:00-06:00 traces. Overnight 27 Nov on v3.1.0 the lights were off from 00:08. Three short FP2 visits at 04:06-04:23 each switched them on and back off within 1-6 min, which confirms the J2 off path live (T1).

jobs.title: Living room v3.3.0: manual change pause and manual off respected
jobs.notes: Commits 400e680, 29ae0c3, ef8e8a6, 483ccef. Review 1: P0 fixed (target_effect was rendered after the update lists); P2 fixed (bulb colour always counts as manual). Two P1s showed that stateless manual-off detection cannot tell who switched the lights off, so the D20 fallback applies: Martin chose one input_boolean per room (auto_off_helper). Review 2 of the helper: P1 fixed (helper cleared only after the light calls). P1 fixed (a light change more than 30 s after our off counts as manual, which needs no self-trigger). P1 declined: override resume re-lights an occupied dark room even after a manual off, by design and documented. P2 kept: the helper is set before light.turn_off, so a failed call leaves the helper on and the next update resets it. Decided by orchestrator: tolerance 5 % brightness / 150 K; the night dim level counts as ours; a colour mode counts as manual; profile starts at 06:00 and the 4 profile times re-apply to every lit light. Deploy prerequisite: create input_boolean.living_room_lights_auto_off in HA. Note: during this job another process edited bedroom_precool.yaml, the LG deploy JSON and 2 precool/LG tests in this checkout; those are not part of J4 (one accidental staging was undone). Lighting tests 298+ passed. Added on 2026-11-27 at Martin's request (movie and dinner-party mode): the override is wired to input_boolean.living_room_manual_mode, with auto-resume once both sensors have been clear for override_timeout = 30 min (FP300 ignored in the night window). Commit 5b16810. Codex review 3: no findings. Deploy prerequisite: create input_boolean.living_room_manual_mode too.
